'''CardTable''' was a downloadable program for playing card games on a computer, which ''Star Wars'' CCG players used for online play in the years 2003 to 2005.<ref name="pcf-1264-23404">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23404#23404 Summer Classics Online 2003], retnuhytnuob, Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (6 April 2003). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041105213359/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=23404%26amp Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="pcf-4504-61387">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=61387#61387 Portland, OR players?], Raphael Asselin (1st SWCCG World Champion), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (1 February 2005). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20050218090532/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=61739%26amp Internet Archive]</ref>

== Use for Star Wars CCG ==

In April 2003 the "Summer Classics Online 2003", an online [[Classic]] format tournament announced on the Players Committee forum, was played on CardTable. The announcement recommended version 1.12 of the program over the 1.13 beta because it saved and loaded decks better, and noted that it ran on PCs but not on Macs or Unix. Players got the ''Star Wars'' CCG card data file (CDF) from the Yahoo group "playcardtable" and the card images, set by set, from the Yahoo group "moswccgplayers", unzipped them into the CardTable folder, and built their decks in the program's Deckbuilder.<ref name="pcf-1264-23404" />

In August 2004 [[Scott Armstrong]] and [[Michael Phelps]] started the Yahoo group "swccgplayer" to build a CardTable tournament scene, planning an open-format tournament with no banned cards to begin by 1 October 2004 at the latest.<ref name="pcf-3909-53221">[http://www.swccgpc.com/forums/viewtopic.php?p=53221#53221 Worldwide Tournament], Scott Armstrong (furhead16), Players Committee forum, swccgpc.com (25 August 2004). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041031063441/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?p=53221%26amp Internet Archive]</ref> In February 2005 [[Raphael Asselin]] recommended CardTable or Holotable to a player who could not find opponents locally, as a way to play people from around the world.<ref name="pcf-4504-61387" />
